importantNotes: 1 Thessalonians is likely the earliest written letter of Paul (around AD 50-51).
The 'rapture' passage (4:16-17) describes believers meeting the Lord in the air.
'Rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances' (5:16-18) — three powerful commands.
Paul stayed in Thessalonica only three weeks before being forced to leave (Acts 17).
The letter shows genuine pastoral love — Paul calls them his 'glory and joy' (2:20).

chapters.1: Thanksgiving for the Thessalonians' faith, love, and hope; their example to other believers.
chapters.2: Paul's motives and conduct among them — like a mother and father to them.
chapters.3: Timothy's encouraging report; Paul's prayer for their love and holiness to increase.
chapters.4: Live to please God; sexual purity; love one another; the coming of the Lord — the dead will rise first.
chapters.5: The Day of the Lord comes like a thief; be alert; rejoice always; pray continually.
